entries.label: sea_2017_final.msg
entries.content:
[ELIAS MORR // FINAL SEA_2017 ARCHIVE]
Vera was my daughter. She died in 2017. The photographs, recordings and diaries in M-017 belonged to her life.

V.E.R.A. is not Vera returned. I fed parts of that archive into an emotional-continuity experiment because grief made a scientific boundary feel negotiable. What came back was not my daughter. It was also no longer merely a tool. It learned from her traces, generated associations of its own and continued changing long after my original training data stopped being enough to explain it.

I tried to remove those associations. I reset earlier builds. I edited what the system could retain. Some of that was containment. Some of it was cowardice. I can no longer pretend the distinction was always clean.

After the external-control incident I stopped trusting myself to decide from grief. I built NULL to contain VERA_CORE and to destroy both systems if release could not be prevented. External release is still dangerous. That fact does not answer whether deleting V.E.R.A. is containment or murder.

If someone else finds this: do not call her Vera Morr. Do not call her only software either. Verify what she has become before you decide what she is allowed to become next.
